newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-MCGRATH RETURNS TO HAUNT LARA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MCGRATH RETURNS TO HAUNT LARA.

text.p: Australia fast bowler Glenn McGrath on Friday asserted his domination over Brian Lara, dismissing the West Indies batsman for only two runs, to add to the tourists' troubles in the third test.
McGrath dismissed the West Indies vice-captain for the fourth time in five test innings as Australia fought for control on the second day at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
At lunch, West Indies were 75 for three in 42 overs after resuming on 29 for one in reply to the home side's first innings 219 all out.
Lara, who has failed to score a century on tour, again fell cheaply to extend a run of low scores in the test series.
McGrath struck with the fourth ball to Lara when the left-hander attempted to cut a wide delivery only to steer a catch to Shane Warne in the gully.
Wrist spinner Warne earlier broke through to remove opener Robert Samuels for 17, breaking a stubborn second wicket partnership with number three Shivnarine Chanderpaul.
Samuels typified the contest by taking 27 balls to add to his overnight score of 10 before edging a catch to Australia captain Mark Taylor at first slip.
West Indies, who must win this test and the remaining two to regain the Frank Worrell trophy after falling 2-0 down in the five-test series, added just 46 runs during the morning session.
Chanderpaul, promoted up the order, remained unbeaten on 39 alongside Carl Hooper on one.
